It’s important to always hire an electrician licensed in your state. You can verify an electrician’s license by visiting your state’s licensing board and looking up their full name, business name, and/or license number. Ensure their license is still active and valid, and watch out for red flags (like too many complaints).
In addition to verifying their license, do the following before hiring an electrician:

Hire a professional electrician if you experience any of these common issues and [electrical hazards](https://www.thumbtack.com/guide/content/10-emergency-home-repairs-you-need-to-prepare-for-now-390327129028845571#8Electricalhazardsandfirerisks):
Electricians in your area may offer 24-hour emergency services, but their availability may vary. You’ll need to contact pros in your area and ask about their rates and response times.
- **Give the electrician details about the problem.** Describe the issue in detail. Explain to them what you see, hear, and even smell.
- **Remove obstacles and obstructions from the work site.** Ensure the electrician has a clutter-free area to work, and that they can easily access your electrical system components.
- **Keep pets and children away.** This will help ensure their safety and allow the electrician to focus on their work without distractions.

Avoid DIY-ing any electrical work to ensure your safety. Instead, hire a licensed electrician. Electrical projects contain many [hazards](https://www.thumbtack.com/guide/content/electrical-home-maintenance-safety-tips-414292159297634306), including electrical fires and shocks. A licensed professional has the proper safety equipment and the expertise to help prevent damage and injuries when performing repairs.
